title: Salmon Rillettes
description:
A light but rich tasting spread made with fresh and smoked salmon. This is an adaptation of David Lebovitz’s adaptation of Susan Loomis’s salmon rillettes. You can serve the spread with sliced bread or crackers, spoon onto endive leaves, cucumber rounds or squares of red and green pepper, or use as a filling for miniature bell peppers.
Smoked and poached fish costar in silky, sophisticated, and simple-to-make rillettes. Swiped across a toasted baguette slice at a party, salmon rillettes feel extravagant. But the cook is the one who experiences its true luxury—the savory spread comes together quickly from a handful of ingredients, and it can be made up to a day ahead. Simply pull it out of the fridge and serve it as a cocktail hour nibble or pack it into a jar as a host gift.
ingredients: 5 ounces smoked salmon, cut into thin strips, then into 1/4-inch pieces
2 tablespoon unsalted butter, at room temperature
2 tablespoon crème fraîche (or omit and use 5 tablespoons yogurt)
directions: Bring some water to boil with various spices – herbs de Provence, onion, garlic, basil, etc. Season salmon with salt and pepper, place it in the pot, cover, and remove the pot from the heat. After 10 minutes, it should be just cooked through and easy to flake apart, but moist.
Remove from heat and allow to cool.
Process the smoked salmon and butter in a food processor until a smooth paste forms, 15 to 20 seconds, scrapping down the sides of a bowl after 10 seconds.
Add yogurt, mustard, crème fraiche, and a little salt, and blend until well combined, about another 10 seconds.

Flake the salmon (without the skin) into a medium-size bowl and add smoked salmon mixture. Using a fork, mash the two together until well combined and salmon has broken down into little pieces. Add lemon juice to taste and the chives, and gently mix together well. Add pepper (salt?) and mix together. Chill for 1 to 2 hours. Allow to come to room temperature before serving.
Either spoon onto endive leaves or other vegetables, or serve with toasted bread or crackers.
notes:
Tip:
Advance preparation: The rillettes will keep for 2 days in the refrigerator and can be frozen.
